issues.title: Bitpacking select: decode only the selected rows' blocks for filtered scans
issues.hypothesis: In q09 the lineitem scan applies the part BF on l_partkey (60M rows in, 3.27M out, about 5.5%) and then fetches 4 non-filter BitPacking columns: l_orderkey (DELTA_FOR), l_quantity, l_extendedprice, l_discount (all FOR). Bitpacking registers no `select` callback (bitpacking.cpp GetBitpackingFunction sets only scan/scan_partial/fetch_row/skip), so StandardColumnData::Select (standard_column_data.cpp:103) takes the ColumnData::Select fallback. That fallback decodes all 2048 values, applies FOR to all of them, and then Slices, which hands a dictionary vector to every downstream operator. Measured with 5-run batches: lineitem JOIN part (BF) with count(*) only is 21.5 ms/run. Adding sums over l_extendedprice, l_suppkey, l_orderkey, l_quantity and l_discount gives 44.5 ms/run, so the non-filter columns cost about 20 ms of q09's roughly 83 ms/run. (l_suppkey has a min/max dynamic filter, so it is decoded as a filter column either way.) A select that unpacks only the 32-value algorithm blocks that contain a selected row, writes only the selected values into a compact flat vector, and skips the Slice should remove a large part of that cost.
issues.plan: In src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp add `template <class T, class T_S = MakeSigned<T>::type, class T_U = ...> void BitpackingSelect(ColumnSegment &segment, ColumnScanState &state, idx_t vector_count, Vector &result, const SelectionVector &sel, idx_t sel_count)`, using the signature of RLESelect (rle.cpp:427) and DictFSSTSelect, and register it in GetBitpackingFunction with `bitpacking.select = BitpackingSelect<T>;`. Implementation: mirror the loop in BitpackingScanPartial (bitpacking.cpp:775), walking the vector_count positions through metadata groups (LoadNextGroup when current_group_offset == BITPACKING_METADATA_GROUP_SIZE) and 32-value algorithm groups, while keeping a cursor into sel. The sel indices are ascending; throw an InternalException if they are not, as RLE does. Per mode: CONSTANT writes current_constant for the selected indices in range. CONSTANT_DELTA writes constant*offset + FOR for the selected indices. FOR: if no selected index falls in this 32-block, only advance current_group_offset (no unpack); otherwise UnPackBlock into scan_state.decompression_buffer and write buffer[off]+FOR for each selected index in the block. DELTA_FOR: always unpack, ApplyFrameOfReference plus DeltaDecode into the decompression buffer (the delta chain needs every value), update current_delta_offset, and copy out the selected values. At the end the scan state must sit exactly vector_count positions further on, the same as after BitpackingScan. Set the result to FLAT_VECTOR with result_data[i] for i < sel_count. Validity is handled separately in StandardColumnData::Select (it already requires validity_has_select), so do not touch it. Test with dbe-tool sql: filtered scans comparing sum/min/max of FOR, DELTA_FOR and constant columns (e.g. sorted keys, low-cardinality ints, dates, decimals) against the same query with the filter wrapped so it is not pushed down. Use selectivities of 0.1%, 5%, 50% and 99%, and also run a query on a column that contains NULLs.
issues.expected_gain: q09: about 5-12% (the measured 20 ms of non-filter column decode at 5.5% selectivity; about 16% of FOR blocks are skipped entirely, and the full-vector FOR pass, the 2048-wide writes and the dictionary Slice all go away).
issues.generality: Any scan of a BitPacking integer, date or decimal column (the default for most integer data) that has a selective pushed filter or a dynamic join filter (BF or min/max) on another column. At 1% selectivity about 72% of the blocks are skipped. This is common in star-schema fact scans. Downstream operators also get flat vectors instead of dictionary slices. Possible slowdown: near-100% selectivity adds a little per-index bookkeeping compared with a straight decode. The implementer may fall back to scan+copy when sel_count > about 0.75*vector_count.
issues.risk: Medium-low. It is an isolated new callback, but scan-state advancement must match Scan exactly. An off-by-one in group or offset handling would corrupt later vectors, especially at metadata-group boundaries (offset not aligned to 2048) and in DELTA_FOR. It only runs when StandardColumnData::Select sees a full-vector scan and a validity select exists.
